# PART 1 — The four named questions, answered from current code

## (a) The straggler stop aborts the third draft — what is the right fix now?

**Mechanism, confirmed end to end.**

- `crates/goose-cli/src/commands/swarm.rs:2896` — `should_arm_straggler_grace(n, valid) = n >= 3 && valid >= 2 && valid >= n - 1`. On this fleet `n == 3` (clamped to distinct draft models at `:14457`), so the grace arms **the instant the 2nd valid draft lands**, and the 3rd is aborted 45s later (`straggler_grace_secs` default 45, `:2881`).
- `straggler_stop` is **baked ON** in the config default: `:1195 straggler_stop: Some(true)`.
- So in the common case `valid1.len() == 2`.
- `crates/goose-cli/src/commands/swarm.rs:14716` — `let (best2, _) = best_subset_agreement(&valid1, converge, 2);`
- `crates/goose-cli/src/commands/swarm.rs:11752` — `best_subset_agreement` opens with `let k = k.max(2); if n <= k { return plan_agreement(candidates, converge); }`.

**With 2 drafts, `n <= k` is `2 <= 2` → it returns `plan_agreement` verbatim → `best2 == conf1` exactly → the `if best2 > conf1` lift at `:14770` is arithmetically unreachable.** a9f43543d is a no-op by construction whenever straggler-stop bites, which is precisely the reported 80%.

**And it is worse than "the pool-invariant is a no-op" — the same collapse disables the entire ladder mechanism.**

1. **`consensus_k` is dead too.** At `:25352` the caller passes `consensus_k = Some(best_of_n)` only when retarget grew the pool. That value feeds `:14659`'s `best_subset_agreement(&valid1, converge, k)` — same `n <= k` fallback, same 2-draft pool. The lever's stated premise ("grow the pool, the tightest k-subset can only raise the metric", doc at `:11746`) **cannot fire on any rung**.
2. **The redraft ladder cannot climb.** Every rung re-enters `parallel_plan` → `draft_round` → the same straggler collector. `effective_best_of_n` escalates 3→4→5→6 (`:25492`) but `n = requested_n.min(draft_models.len())` caps at 3 distinct models (`:14457`), then straggler-stop cuts to 2. That is the mechanical explanation for the archived `84 → 70 → 70 → 52` and for why the stall guard had to be invented.
3. **It also raises the bar for `diverse_plan`.** `structural_convergence` (`:11901`) uses `majority = n/2 + 1`. At n=3 majority is 2; at n=2 majority is **2 = unanimity**. Losing the third draft makes `struct_conv` strictly harder to clear — so the "would_skip_ladder 7/7 TRUE" reading was measured on a *harsher* metric than the one a full pool would produce. Same for `consensus_backbone` (`:11790`).

**The right fix (concrete): gate the arming on whether the quorum already decides the ladder.**

Today the grace arms on *count*. It should arm on *count AND the fact that the third draft cannot change the outcome*. The call site already has everything needed — `draft_is_valid` at `:14545` already does `specs_from_plan_json(j) → Dag::from_specs(s)`, i.e. it already parses to `Vec<TaskSpec>`.

Change `collect_drafts_with_straggler_stop`'s validity closure from `Fn(&str) -> bool` to one that returns the parsed specs, accumulate them, and arm only when:

```
should_arm_straggler_grace(n, valid)
  && plan_agreement(&valid_specs_so_far, converge).0 >= ask_floor
```

- If the two in-hand drafts **already clear the floor**, the third draft cannot trigger a ladder → abort it, keep today's speed win in full.
- If the two in-hand drafts are **below the floor**, the third draft is the single cheapest thing that can avoid a **~25-minute ladder round** (the measured cost recorded at `:14752`). Waiting up to `draft_timeout` for it is strictly cheaper in expectation, and it is exactly the case where the pool-invariant lift and `best_subset_agreement` become live again.

This is asymmetric in the right direction: it can only *extend* the draft wait in the branch where the alternative is a 25-minute serial rung, and it is a **no-op at one node** (`n < 3` never arms; `agreement_conf` is `None` at n==1 so the confidence gate is never entered — the stronger route documented at `:14757`).

**Secondary, cheaper variant if you want zero risk to the draft phase:** leave arming alone and instead make the lift honest by **not asking a 2-pool for a 2-subset**. Compute `best2` only when `valid1.len() > 2`, and emit `pool_invariant_inert: true` with `drafts` when it isn't — today `plan_convergence` emits `pool_invariant_applied: false` (`:14736`) which reads identically to "the pool penalty didn't bite" when the truth is "the measure could not run". That is instrumentation only; it makes the 20% visible rather than fixing it.

**Expected axis:** speed primarily (removes 1–4 rungs × ~25 min from 3-node runs), quality secondarily (the ladder's last rung is what ships on any asking run — `:25191`). **Confidence: high** on the mechanism (read directly off `n <= k`), **medium** on the size of the win (the commit at `:14766` correctly warns runs are not randomised into laddering).

## (b) The judge's ~165 invocations doing nothing — make idle supervision CONTRIBUTE to Tier B

**Where the invocations go, in current code.** `crates/goose-cli/src/commands/swarm.rs:19107-19120`: when no device is idle, `judge_model_id` is empty and the judge returns `JudgeOutcome::ok()` with reason `no_idle_device`. The in-source measurement at `:19143` records the consequence: **814 of 851 verdicts (95.7%) were `confidence 1.0` + empty hint — the semantic review ran 4.3% of the time.** The judge is not deciding "ok"; it is mostly never asked. 7a2a2541d then made the *remaining* verdicts non-inert by keeping their hint (`scheduler.rs:247 observed_hint_worth_keeping`), which is the correct fix for the cap-exhausted case but does nothing for the 95.7%.

**Why it cannot contribute to Tier B as built.** `Verdict` (`crates/goose-swarm/src/judge.rs:18`) has exactly one Tier-B-shaped member, `SpecDrift`, and *every* problem verdict's only action is kill-and-redispatch or terminal-fail (`scheduler.rs:1634 apply_judge_outcome`). A supervisor whose sole output type is "stop this worker" structurally cannot emit "the summary endpoint omits the totals row". The judge is a **liveness** instrument pointed at a **conformance** score.

**The instrument that IS Tier-B-shaped already exists and is under-aimed.** `PreReviewer` (`judge.rs:344`) writes findings to `.swarm/prereview/<task>.json` (`swarm.rs:19387`), and `read_prereview_findings` (`:18607`) injects them into the sink prompt under a mandatory-repair heading (`:22178`). Pre-review is **default ON** (`:26466`, opt out with `GOOSE_SWARM_PREREVIEW=0`). But its system prompt (`:19345`) asks for exactly two defect classes: *wrong default/primary path* and *built-but-not-wired*. Neither is pagination, chronological order, UTC bounds, totals, or input validation.

Meanwhile `REVIEW_DIMENSIONS` (`:10861`) — five rotating dimensions with real briefs (correctness / wiring / interface / edge-cases / domain-conventions), plus `DOMAIN_PITFALLS` external ground truth (`:10904`) — is wired **only** to `idle_dimension_review` (`:19402`), reachable only through `sink_review`, whose own commit a3fdfce02 says it "**has never run anywhere**" and was shipped as reachability, not as a default.

**Concrete fix: turn the judge's dead idle slot into a spec-clause pre-review, and give the pre-reviewer the Tier-B dimension list.**

1. **Add a `Verdict`-free path.** In `Judge::judge` at `swarm.rs:19107`, the `no_idle_device` branch is correct (don't queue behind a busy worker). The waste is upstream in `scheduler.rs`'s `pick_judge_target` — it selects a judge target *before* knowing a device is free. Invert: when no device is free, do not call `judge` at all (saves the ~165 no-op calls outright); when one IS free and no in-flight worker needs judging, the scheduler already prefers `pre_review` (`scheduler.rs:2700`). That is a pure-speed cleanup.
2. **The quality half — make pre-review dimension-rotating and spec-clause-anchored.** `pre_review` (`:19299`) already receives `goal` (the full amended spec — `:26533` confirms this copy carries the amendment) and the subtask description. Rotate `REVIEW_DIMENSIONS` into its system prompt the same way `idle_dimension_review` does, and **add a sixth dimension: `spec-conformance`** — "for each numbered requirement in the GOAL that these files are responsible for, state whether the code satisfies it; flag pagination/cursoring, UTC boundary handling, chronological ordering, totals/aggregate arithmetic, row shape, and input validation as ISSUES when the code contradicts the spec's own sentence." That is the literal Tier B list and no existing dimension covers it.
3. **Escalate a repeated `SpecDrift` into a pre-review finding.** `observed_hint_worth_keeping` already preserves the hint. Extend it: when the same task draws a `SpecDrift` verdict twice, also write the hint to `.swarm/prereview/<task>.json` in `PreReviewOutput` shape. Then a diagnosis the judge cannot act on becomes a **finding integrate-verify is contractually required to confirm and fix** (`:22163`), rather than a hint for a re-dispatch that will never happen.

**Expected axis:** quality (Tier B directly — this is the only idle-node instrument whose output reaches the sink as a repair order), plus a small speed gain from dropping the no-op calls. **Confidence: high** that the current judge cannot contribute to Tier B (verdict enum + action branches are exhaustive and I read both); **medium** that dimension-rotated pre-review converts to score — the prompt is right but the reviewer is the same weak local model, and `pre_review` has one measured false-finding incident already (the head-truncation phantom recorded at `:19310`, since fixed by `review_file_excerpt`).

## (c) Replan injects unasked work in 85% of 3-node runs — the additive-only constraint

**What is already there.** 46f0c84ca added `replan_has_enough_dag_left(mandatory_incomplete, mandatory_total)` (`crates/goose-swarm/src/scheduler.rs:317`) = `mandatory_total == 0 || mandatory_incomplete * 4 >= mandatory_total` — a **fraction**, wired into the replan condition at `:2530`, alongside `idle_capacity() >= 2`, `replans_done < max_replans`, `!sink_in_flight()`. `mandatory_incomplete`/`mandatory_total` (`:663`/`:679`) correctly exclude `bonus_ids` — load-bearing, because the DAG grows with each injection.

**The remaining hole, stated by its own author.** "n3-r0's injection came earlier with more DAG outstanding and this gate would have **ALLOWED** it. Two of three measured tails addressed, one not." The gate bounds *when* you may inject; it does nothing about *what happens after*.

**The structural defect: a bonus task can still be the last task in the run.** `bonus_ids` only makes a bonus **failure** non-fatal (`:374`, `:2574`). The main loop terminates on `incomplete_count()` (`:612`) — **which counts bonus tasks**. So a bonus task injected legally at 30% remaining, that then runs 27 minutes, still sets the run's wall clock. `dynamic_replan` is `true` by default (`swarm.rs:1204`).

**The constraint that makes replan additive-only, and why the naive version was correctly rejected.** 46f0c84ca refused "stop the bonus worker at the tail" for a real reason: *a half-written Python test file breaks pytest collection wholesale — worse than no file.* That objection is entirely about **where the bonus worker writes**, not about whether it may be stopped.

So: **make bonus work staged, then abortable.**

1. Dispatch every bonus task with its owned files rooted in a scratch overlay (`.swarm/bonus/<task-id>/`), not the tree.
2. On bonus **completion**, atomically move its files into the tree (the files are already file-partitioned and non-overlapping — `held_files`/`held_by` at `:1948` guarantee it).
3. Once every **mandatory** task is terminal, abort any in-flight bonus task and discard its scratch dir.

With (1)+(2), aborting a bonus worker leaves **zero** partial files in the tree — the exact objection dissolves — and (3) makes the invariant literal: *a bonus task can add score and can never add wall-clock.* That is "additive-only" as an engine property rather than a heuristic window.

A cheaper interim (no overlay): keep the fractional gate but **also require that the bonus task's expected duration fits inside the remaining mandatory critical path**, using the per-host EWMA the scheduler already maintains for `dispatch_prefers_fastest_node` (`:319`, and the speed weights at `:789`). Weaker — it is a prediction, not an invariant — but it is a ~20-line change and it would have refused n3-r0.

**Expected axis:** speed floor (this is the named mechanism by which 3 nodes are *slower* than 1 — a 1-node run never reaches `idle_capacity() >= 2` and so never grows a bonus tail, `:299`), quality neutral-to-positive (bonus tests still land when they finish in time; the cell that scored 0.9033 keeps them). **Confidence: high** on the defect (the termination condition counts bonus tasks — read directly); **medium-high** on the overlay fix (it touches dispatch cwd handling, which I did not fully trace).

## (d) The 43-char split-child statement — what does split buy WITH a real statement?

**The fix is already written and switched off.** `crates/goose-swarm/src/scheduler.rs:76 child_description(parent_id, parent_desc, child, inherit_spec)`:

- `inherit_spec == false` → `format!("(split of {parent_id}) {}", child.id)` — literally the 43-char string, pinned by a test at `:2812` (`"(split of data-model-persistence) note-store"`, 43 chars, against a **2038-char** parent spec).
- `inherit_spec == true` → a file-scope header naming exactly the child's files, an explicit "the other files belong to other workers, do not create/edit/wait for them", then **the parent's full spec as context**.

The gate is `split_inherit_spec_enabled()` (`:58`), reading `GOOSE_SWARM_SPLIT_INHERIT_SPEC`, **default OFF** — and unlike almost every sibling lever it has **no config bridge**, so a desktop launch (which cannot set env, per a3fdfce02's finding) can never turn it on. Introduced by 418a421f7 ("stop the split from throwing away the spec PLAN just paid 40% to write").

**Why this matters more than it looks.** Split is **default ON** — `swarm.rs:18960`: `GOOSE_SWARM_SPLIT` env, else `load_config().split.unwrap_or(true)`. So every split that fires today hands a worker a 43-character instruction, and the run has *already paid* for the parent's spec: `detail_budget_secs` (`:2843`) is the fan that authors it, and the in-source measurement there ties spec length directly to score — *"the run where `meridian` shipped a 122-char brief scored 42.7% while the run where it got a 1497-char spec scored 88.7%."*

The one instrument that could size the delta was added in this window: F717/C12(b) put `description_chars` on `TaskDispatched` (`crates/goose-swarm/src/event.rs`, `scheduler.rs`), explicitly so "both arms of a lever that has never been observed" become comparable.

**Concrete fix.** Make it reachable and default it ON: add `split_inherit_spec: Option<bool>` to `SwarmConfig`, bridge it in `run_swarm` by **writing the env var `split_inherit_spec_enabled()` already reads** (the bridge shape a3fdfce02 established, so producer and reporter cannot disagree), and flip the `unwrap_or` to `true`. The risk the lever introduces is named in its own test at `:2856` — the child now reads about files it must not touch — and is mitigated by ordering (scope guard before spec, asserted by that test) and bounded by `apply_split`'s partition validation (`:1954`: disjoint, covering, no foreign files, no sibling cycles, no-op on any violation).

**What split buys with a real statement.** Today's +0.036 is bought by *parallelism alone* — three workers finishing a too-big task faster, each guessing what its file should contain from an id like `note-store`. Tier B is precisely the class of requirement that lives in the spec prose (pagination, UTC bounds, totals, row shape) and is **unrecoverable from a filename**. The 43-char arm should be losing Tier B points on every split child; the +0.036 is the parallelism gain *net of* that loss. **Confidence: high** that the statement is the 43-char string and that split is default-ON (both read directly); **medium** on the size — no archived run carries `description_chars` yet, which is exactly why F717 added it. **This is the cheapest quality change on the board: the code is written, tested both arms, and off.**

# PART 2 — Per-phase delta and next defect

### 1. research / scouts

**Changed since Aug 7:** 02ba537ed (F718/C7) — `scout_lookup(has_mcp, has_docs) -> ScoutLookup` extracted as a pure function the call site matches on (`swarm.rs:~3438`), behind `GOOSE_SWARM_SCOUT_DOC_URLS` **default OFF**. Fixes one boolean answering two questions: a scout with no MCP extension still holds a shell, and 59 of 77 scouts (77%) fetched a URL while under an explicit instruction that they could not.

**Top remaining defect:** the fix is **off**, so the engine still tells 77% of scouts a falsehood about their own capability, on a spec that names its vendor documentation URL. Secondary: scouts collect via `collect_fleet_with_straggler_stop` (`:18347`) with the same `n >= 3 && valid >= n-1` predicate — on a 3-scout fanout the third scout is *always* the one aborted, and unlike drafts there is no validity gate at all (`Some(Err(_)) => done += 1` at `:2986` counts a **panicked** task toward the quorum, so two failures can arm the grace and abort the only healthy scout).

**Concrete fix:** (i) config-bridge + default-on `GOOSE_SWARM_SCOUT_DOC_URLS`; (ii) in `collect_fleet_with_straggler_stop`, count only `Ok(r)` toward the arming quorum — an errored task is not a result. **Axis:** quality (grounding feeds Tier B's vendor-contract clauses). **Confidence:** high on (ii) — the `Err` arm increments `done` and the doc comment claims "every completed task is a usable result", which an `Err` is not.

### 2. clarify

**Changed since Aug 7:** nothing directly. Adjacent: `answers_win_floor` and `ask_away` remain as-is (`:25245`, `:25253`).

**Top remaining defect:** `spec_clarity_confidence` (`:19366`) combines with structural agreement by MIN (`:11401`), so the same collapsed 2-draft agreement from (a) drags the clarify decision down with it. A run whose drafts were *cut* below the floor asks the user questions it did not need to ask, and — per `:25190` — **an answered ask nulls `best_plan`, so the ladder's last rung ships**. The straggler defect therefore reaches the clarify phase and turns a speed optimisation into a quality regression.

**Concrete fix:** fold into (a); no separate change. Instrument first: emit `binding_signal` alongside `drafts` on the clarify decision so "asked because the spec is vague" and "asked because we scored 2 drafts" are distinguishable. **Axis:** quality. **Confidence:** medium-high (the MIN combination is explicit at `:11401`; I did not trace every clarify caller).

### 3. skeleton vote + retarget ladder — **highest leverage in the run**

**Changed since Aug 7:** a9f43543d (act on the pool-invariant at round 1); 9a49deda0 (`spec_contract` inconclusive reasons); 81c11c21a (instrument the second silent window — `skeleton_drafts` with `requested`/`dead`/`straggler_aborted`/`secs`/`chars`, `:14608`); a3d3b9443 (F717: `requested_best_of_n`, `distinct_draft_models`, `clamped`; corrected the "one node drafts 2" falsehood at four sites); 3654f9c3c (F707: `would_skip_ladder` vs `would_skip_ladder_prelift` — the shadow and the branch had drifted apart *because of* a9f43543d); 9d79cae92 (F706: stall-lever comments described a default the code does not have).

**Top remaining defect:** the ladder **cannot climb**, for three compounding reasons all live in current code: straggler-stop caps the scored pool at 2 (`:2896`), `best_subset_agreement` degenerates to `plan_agreement` at `n <= k` (`:11752`), and `RETARGET_MAX_N = 6` (`:11359`) exceeds `draft_models.len() == 3` so rungs 4–6 request drafts that cannot exist (`:14453` says so explicitly and the clamp at `:14457` enforces it). Each rung costs ~25 min of the whole fleet.

**Concrete fix:** (a)'s agreement-gated arming, **plus** clamp `RETARGET_MAX_N` to `draft_models.len()` at the escalation site (`:25492`) so a rung that cannot add a distinct draft is never spent. The stall guard (`retarget_stall_guard`, default `true` at `:1250`) is a downstream mitigation for the same disease — with the clamp it becomes mostly redundant. **Axis:** speed (the ladder is "the ENTIRE three-node planning tax", `:14754`) then quality. **Confidence:** high on mechanism, medium on magnitude.

### 4. detail fan

**Changed since Aug 7:** just outside the window (32f95a421) but now live and load-bearing — `detail_budget_secs()` (`:2843`) derives from `worker_timeout_secs.max(75)` clamped to `[30, 900]` instead of the hardcoded 75. With `worker_timeout_secs` baked at 900, **the detail budget went 75s → 900s, a 12× increase.**

**Top remaining defect:** `straggler_stop_degrade` (`:187`, covering the CONTRACTS and DETAIL fanouts) is **default OFF** (`:1197 straggler_stop_degrade: None`). So the detail fan **awaits all**, and one slow detail call can now block the fan for **900 seconds** where it previously cost 75. The quality argument for the raise is strong (25 of 25 detail failures were timeouts; a lost detail call ships a 95-char spec for a module Tier C grades) — but it was landed with the tail-risk knob off, which is a direct hit on the speed floor and it scales with fleet size (more subtasks = more chances of one straggler).

**Concrete fix:** turn `straggler_stop_degrade` ON for the DETAIL fanout specifically, with grace derived from the *median* completed detail call rather than the flat 45s. A stopped detail straggler degrades to the architect's one-line brief — exactly the pre-raise behaviour — so the worst case is bounded at the old outcome for one subtask instead of 900s for the whole fan. **Axis:** speed floor. **Confidence:** high that the exposure exists (both the budget raise and the default-off gate are read directly); medium on whether it has bitten yet — this is a *new* exposure, so archived runs will not show it.

### 5. contracts (probe_post)

**Changed since Aug 7:** c8a63a34e (F738) added `spec_post_endpoints` (`:3525`) + pure `repeated_post_verdict` (`:3597`) that the call site matches on, behind `GOOSE_SWARM_PROBE_ADVERTISED_POST`; 23193cef3 (F740) added the `NotCheap` arm after the first version **scored the failing app as a PASS** on `inserted:0` + flat `total`, and corrected the remediation text (the apps *do* send `If-None-Match`; they replay one stored ETag on the next page where it can never match).

**Top remaining defects, three, all in code added in the last 48 hours:**

1. **The gate is default OFF.** `swarm.rs:18021`: `if swarm_gate("GOOSE_SWARM_PROBE_ADVERTISED_POST", false)`. The largest single block on the defect board (16.3% of remaining loss on the full n=8 corpus, rank 1 and 2, per F740's own correction) is behind a flag nothing sets, and there is **no config bridge** — same shape as the `sink_review` defect a3fdfce02 fixed three days ago.
2. **Probing one POST silences the honesty admission about all the others.** `:18074`: `let unprobed = if post_probed > 0 { Vec::new() } else { spec_unprobed_advertised(spec) };` — and `spec_unprobed_advertised` (`:17708`) returns **every non-GET** method. A spec advertising `POST /api/sync` + `DELETE /api/cache` that probes only the POST now reports *zero* unprobed endpoints. This is precisely the "the more candidly this check explained itself, the more certainly it reported success" failure the sibling code at `:26880` was rewritten to kill.
3. **The probe can manufacture a false `Duplicates` finding.** The two POSTs are issued back to back with `curl -m 20` inside `smoke_output(call(), 25)` (`:18027`). On a first-ever sync of 247 pages, curl abandons the request at 20s — **the server keeps syncing**. The second POST then starts *concurrently with the first still running*, and a concurrent double-sync is exactly how `total` grows. The engine would report "POST is NOT idempotent — total went X → Y" against a correct app, and that finding goes straight into `verdict.findings` (`:26887`) and drives the fix loop. This is the "first WRITE the contract gate has ever issued" risk the commit named, arriving through timing rather than through the verdict logic.

**Concrete fixes:** (1) config-bridge it and default ON; (2) `unprobed` = advertised non-GET **minus the paths actually probed**, not a boolean suppression; (3) raise the POST timeout to the sync budget and, critically, **require the first call to have completed** before issuing the second — on a first-call timeout, push `inconclusive` and skip the second entirely. **Axis:** quality (rank-1 defect block), with (3) as a correctness guard on the gate itself. **Confidence:** high on (1) and (2) (read directly); medium-high on (3) — it depends on the app's sync duration exceeding 20s, which the spec's 247 pages plus vendor throttling makes likely but which I did not measure.

**Concrete fix:** §b and §d as written. Order them: **§d first** (the code exists, it is a flag flip plus a config bridge), **§b second** (a prompt change to `pre_review` plus a sixth dimension). **Axis:** quality. **Confidence:** high on §d, medium on §b.

### 7. verify layer (`fan_verify`)

**Changed since Aug 7:** nothing in the window.

**Top remaining defect:** `fan_verify` shards by MODULE (`:3770`) and is default ON (`:1297`). The in-source note at `:704` records that this "left one node [doing the work] while the other two idled" — checking `get` says nothing about checking `compact`. The module axis is orthogonal to how Tier B is *scored* (behaviour clauses, not modules), so a `verify::<M>` can be green on every module while the app fails sync completeness end to end.

**Concrete fix:** none proposed independently — it is subsumed by §b's `spec-conformance` dimension and by the e2e oracle below, both of which shard on the axis the score actually uses. Flagging it so it is not mistaken for coverage. **Axis:** quality. **Confidence:** medium (I read the split function and its doc, not a live run's shard reports).

### 8. e2e shards

**Changed since Aug 7:** nothing in the window; but the *reason* it exists is directly relevant. `:361-376` records the defect: three shards each derived a **different** command list (lengths 1, 1, 3), so the modulo partition was neither disjoint nor complete, and a shard with an empty slice **reported clean**. `e2e_oracle` (default ON, `:1244`) now hands the engine-enumerated advertised surface to each shard (`e2e_shard_spec`, `:3626`), and `fan_e2e_split` (`:3690`) clamps shard count to `min(oracle.len(), 4)` so empty shards cannot exist.

**Top remaining defect:** the oracle is the **advertised command/endpoint surface**, not the spec's behavioural clauses. A shard verifies that `POST /api/sync` *answers*; nothing in the shard list asks whether it paginated, ordered chronologically, bounded on UTC, or totalled correctly. The `:369` measurement (1, 1, 28, 1 tool calls across four shards — 90% of the work in one, 56.4 min) shows the makespan risk is real and grows with the fleet.

**Concrete fix:** extend the oracle from *commands* to *(command, spec-clause)* pairs — reuse the same spec-clause extraction §b needs, so one parser serves both. Round-robin over pairs rather than commands, which both widens Tier B coverage and evens out the shard imbalance that makes the critical path grow with the fleet. **Axis:** quality primarily, speed floor secondarily. **Confidence:** medium (clause extraction from spec prose is the hard part and does not exist yet).

### 9. integrate-verify sink

**Changed since Aug 7:** 3ca937172 (the owns-nothing `Accept` branch — the largest single change in the window; before it, **not one verdict was reachable** for `integrate-verify`, so the judge's only lever on the join was a kill that redid the entire join from zero); 7abd351cf ("the join owns nothing — the rewrite said so everywhere except the one line that mattered"); a3fdfce02 (`sink_review` made reachable via config, still default OFF); 94530b90d (corrected a false claim about the desktop join cap).

**Top remaining defect:** `sink_review` is the one mechanism aimed squarely at the measured occupancy deficit (**1-node execute occupancy 1.0000, 1.0000; 3-node 0.5535, 0.6678, 0.8256** — five cells, no overlap, dominated by the join running alone) and it is still **default OFF**. a3fdfce02 deliberately shipped reachability without the default, which was correct discipline — but the caveat it recorded is now the decision point: *"filling idle nodes raises occupancy BY CONSTRUCTION. If the review findings do not help the join, this buys a better-looking number and no better app."*

**Concrete fix:** turn `sink_review` ON **only after** §b lands the `spec-conformance` dimension — because `idle_dimension_review` (`:19402`) rotates the *same* `REVIEW_DIMENSIONS` array. With the sixth dimension in place, the idle-fill produces Tier-B findings that `run_swarm` drains and **re-verifies against the final tree** (fail-closed, so a torn read is refuted). Without it, it produces four dimensions the pre-reviewer already covered. **Axis:** quality (and occupancy, which is not the goal). **Confidence:** high that it is off and reachable; medium that it converts — this is the caveat's own falsifier.

### 10. complete / fix tail

**Changed since Aug 7:** d91fd8b96 + caee78c71 (**spec_repair baked ON** — `spec_repair_wave` appeared in **zero** of 13 archived cells; promotion is monotonic by construction via `pick_repair_winner`, and the call-site guard tightened from `!is_empty()` to `len() > 1` so a 1-node fleet is byte-identical); 34359b8b7 (`complete_cap_fitting_rounds` enforces the cap invariant on the **resolved** value — a stale `complete_cap_secs: 1200` in config.yaml had silently reverted the 1200→3000 fix and no test could see it, because the invariant test asserted on the *default*); 9b7eaf4bf (F711/C1 — `is_test_file` is a **basename** predicate and `:3028` passed it a **full path**, so `tests/test_api.py` read as app code and **55% of round-0 findings were dispatched against files nobody grades**; replay across 24 runs: findings 2.75 → 1.62, paired delta 1.12 ± 0.47 = 2.4 SE, the only significant readout this corpus can produce); 50a542bd7 (F712 — tested the SCAN not the predicate, proved discrimination by deleting the filter); 43bfbca (F714 — `cargo check` is not `cargo fmt`); a439447d3 (corrected a false defect story: exhaustion, not slack).

**Top remaining defect:** `complete_rounds` defaults to **2** (`:23720`) and `complete_cap_fitting_rounds` (`:18913`) only guarantees the *budget* fits those 2 rounds. F711 cut round-0 findings by 41% — which means **more runs now exit the fix loop with the app green but Tier B unfixed**, because the findings that survive are the behavioural ones the scan cannot see (the timeout scan, `cross_module_drift`, and `complete_missing_deliverables` are all structural). And the one gate that *can* see Tier B — the POST probe — is off (§5). The risk the F711 commit itself carried forward: *"fewer runs enter repair at all, and three nodes ALREADY skips repair in 5 of 13 runs vs 0 of 11 at one node."*

**Concrete fix:** §5's flag flip is the whole fix here — it is the only thing that puts a Tier-B finding into `verdict.findings` for the repair loop to act on. Turning on `probe_advertised_post` without also having `spec_repair` on would have serialised the extra findings; with `spec_repair` now baked ON and racing twins across the fleet, the two changes are complementary and this is the **one place where three nodes have a documented use** (`:23056`: median 1 finding per round across 31 rounds — no round ever had work for a third node on the *finding* axis, but the *attempt* axis decomposes). **Axis:** quality, at neutral-to-better wall clock. **Confidence:** high on the wiring (traced `run_spec_contract` → `verdict.findings` → fix loop); medium on the score delta — `spec_repair` has never run in any archived cell, so it is untested in the field by its own commit's admission.

**Two meta-observations across the window.** First, the recurring defect shape is *a correct fix landed behind a flag with no config bridge*: `sink_review` (fixed by a3fdfce02), `split_inherit_spec`, `probe_advertised_post`, `scout_doc_urls` — four instances, three still open, and the desktop cannot set env vars. Second, three of the last four commits fixed a **gate that reported success while blind** (`spec_contract`'s `all([])`, `repeated_post_verdict`'s `Idempotent`, `verified` counting nothing) — and `:18074` is the same shape, shipped 15 minutes after the commit that fixed the previous one.
